source_text: Ὅλως δὲ, ἡ ἄνευ πίστεως ἐπὶ τὸ λαλεῖν ἐρχομένη ψυχὴ δια κενῆς ληρήσει, κατ' οὐδενὸς ὑποκειμένου τὸν λόγον προάγουσα. Ἀρχὴ τοίνυν λόγου ἔμφρονος, πίστις ἰσχυρῶς τῇ καρδίᾳ τοῦ λαλοῦντος ἐνιδρυμένη. Ἔπει τα, πόθεν ἡμῖν δυνατὸν τὸ περὶ τὴν πίστιν τέλειον κατορθοῦν, ἐφεξῆς ἐπάγει, λέγων· Ἐγὼ δὲ ἐταπεινώθην σφόδρα. Ὁ γὰρ μὴ ταπεινώσας ἑαυτοῦ τὴν διάνοιαν, μηδὲ κατὰ μίμησιν τοῦ Ἀποστόλου λέγων τὸ, Ἀδελφοὶ, ἐγὼ ἐμαυτὸν οὔπω λογίζομαι κατει ληφέναι, ἀλλὰ περινοῶν οὐσίας Θεοῦ κατάληψιν, καὶ τῷ ἰδίῳ λογισμῷ ἐκμετρῶν τὰ ἀνέφικτα, καὶ τοσοῦτον λογιζόμενος εἶναι τὸν Θεὸν, ὅσον αὐτὸς τῷ λογισμῷ περιέλαβεν· καὶ ὅλως, ὁ τὸν οἰκεῖον νοῦν μέτρον τῶν ὄντων ποιούμενος, οὐ λογιζόμενος, ὅτι ῥᾷόν ἐστι κοτύλῃ μικρᾷ τὴν πᾶσαν θάλασσαν ἐκμετρῆσαι, ἢ τῷ ἀνθρωπίνῳ νῷ τῆς ἀφάτου μεγαλειότητος τοῦ Θεοῦ περιδράξασθαι, εἰκῆ φυσιούμενος καὶ ἐπαιρό μενος τῇ ματαιότητι τοῦ νοὸς αὐτοῦ, οὐ δύναται λέγειν τὸ, Ἐπίστευσα, διὸ ἐλάλησα· ἐπειδὴ οὐδὲ τὸ ἐφεξῆς ἐπάγειν αὐτῷ δυνατὸν, τὸ, Ἐγὼ δὲ ἐταπεινώθην σφόδρα· τύφῳ γὰρ καὶ ἀλαζονείᾳ συζῇ, καὶ διακένοις ῥήμασιν ἐπαγάλλεται, τὸ ἐκ τῆς πίστεως ἰσχυρὸν μὴ κεκτημένος. Εἶτα οὐχ ἑαυτὸν ταπεινοῖ μόνον, ἀλλὰ καὶ πᾶσαν ὁμοῦ τὴν συγγενῆ ἑαυτῷ καὶ κοινωνὸν τῆς φύσεως ἀνθρωπότητα. Ἐγὼ γὰρ εἶπα, φησὶν, ἐν τῇ ἐκστάσει μου· Πᾶς ἄνθρωπος ψεύστης. Ὥστε ὁ μὴ ἐκ πίστεως βοηθούμενος, ἀλλ' οἴκοθεν ἐπὶ τὸν λόγον ἐρχόμενος, ταῖς ἀνθρωπίναις παρασκευαῖς πρὸς τὴν κατάληψιν τῆς ἀληθείας θαῤῥῶν, ψεύστης ἐστὶ, παραπολὺ τῆς ἀληθείας ἐκπίπτων. Τοῦτον δέ φησιν εἰρηκέναι τὸν λόγον ἐν τῇ ἐκστά σει. Τίς δέ ἐστιν ἡ ἔκστασις; Ἤτοι ὅτι περιβλεψάμενος τὴν ἀνθρωπίνην φύσιν, καὶ διερευνησάμενος, εἴ πού τίς ἐστιν ἐν ἀνθρώποις ἀλήθεια, μηδαμοῦ ταύτην εὑρεῖν δυνηθεὶς ἄνευ τῆς παρὰ τοῦ Θεοῦ βοηθείας, ἔκθαμβος γενόμενος ἐπὶ τῷ παραδόξῳ τοῦ πράγματος, ἐξεβόησα, ὅτι Πᾶς ἄνθρωπος ψεύ στης· ἢ ἐν τῇ ἐκστάσει ἐκείνῃ, ἣν κατεσχηματισάμην ἐπὶ τοῦ Ἀγχοὺς, ἐπιληψίαν καὶ παραφορὰν ὑποκρινάμενος, ἐπειδὴ εἶδον εἰς ἀνάγκην ἐλθόντα ἐμαυτὸν τοῦ καταψεύσασθαι ἐμαυτοῦ, καὶ ἀναπλά σασθαι τὰ μὴ ὄντα, ὑπὲρ τοῦ τὸν ἀπὸ τῶν πολε μίων κίνδυνον ἐκφυγεῖν, τότε εἶπον, ὅτι Πᾶς ἄνθρω πος ψεύστης· κἂν μὴ κατὰ προαίρεσιν, μηδ' ἐπὶ κακῷ τῶν πλησίον, ἀλλὰ πάντως διά τινας περιστατικὰς αἰτίας καταφεύγων ἐπὶ τὸ ψεύδεσθαι. Οὐ μὴν ἑαυτῷ περιπίπτει κατὰ τὸν λόγον ὁ Προφήτης, ὥσπερ τινὲς τῶν σοφιστικῶν ἐπιχειροῦσιν αὐτὸν δι ελέγχειν, τῷ κατὰ περιτροπὴν ἐλέγχῳ ἐμπεπτωκέ ναι λέγοντες τὸν Προφήτην. Εἰ γὰρ πᾶς ἄνθρω πος ψεύστης, ἄνθρωπος δὲ καὶ ὁ Δαβίδ· ψεύστης ἦν καὶ αὐτὸς δηλονότι· εἰ δὲ ψεύστης, οὐ πιστευτέον αὐ τῷ περὶ ὧν ἀποφαίνεται. Μὴ ὄντος δὲ ἀληθοῦς τοῦ λόγου τούτου, μηδὲ ὄντος παντὸς ἀνθρώπου ψεύστου, ἀφήσομεν καὶ τὸν Δαβὶδ τῆς τοῦ ψεύδους αἰτίας. Εἰ δὲ οὐ ψεύδεται, πιστεύσωμεν αὐτῷ περὶ ὧν ἀπο φαίνεται· πιστεύοντες δὲ, πάλιν εἰς τὴν τοῦ ἀπιστεῖν ἀνάγκην περιαχθησόμεθα. Ὥστε εἰ μὲν ἀληθεύει Δαβὶδ, λύει τὸν ἑαυτοῦ λόγον, καὶ ἄνθρωπος ὢν, καὶ μὴ ψευδόμενος· εἰ δὲ ψεύδεται, αὐτόθεν ἔχει τὸ μὴ πιστεύεσθαι· τίς γὰρ προσέξει ψευδολογοῦντι; Ὥστε ἐπειδὴ ἅπαξ ἀπεφήνατο πάντα ἄνθρωπον εἶναι ψεύ στην, ψευδέσθω Δαβὶδ, ἵνα τὸν λόγον πιστώσηται· ἢ ἀληθεύων αὐτὸς, παρέλυσε τὴν ἀπόφασιν.
thought_title: Faith as the foundation of speech, and the meaning of 'every man is a liar'
orientation: Basil is explaining the psalmist's words 'I believed, therefore I spoke' and 'I was greatly humbled,' arguing that only a humble mind grounded in faith can speak truly about God, and then he addresses the psalmist's saying 'Every man is a liar.'
pass_a_gloss: In general, the soul that comes to speaking without faith will babble in vain, advancing its discourse upon no underlying subject. The beginning of rational discourse, then, is faith firmly established in the heart of the speaker. Next, from where it is possible for us to accomplish the perfection concerning faith, he brings in next, saying: 'But I was greatly humbled.' For the one who has not humbled his own mind, nor says in imitation of the Apostle, 'Brothers, I do not yet consider myself to have laid hold,' but instead goes around the comprehension of God's essence, and measures the unattainable things by his own reasoning, and considers God to be as great as he himself has encompassed by reasoning; and in general, the one who makes his own mind the measure of things that exist, not considering that it is easier to measure out the whole sea with a small cup than for the human mind to grasp the ineffable majesty of God, being vainly puffed up and lifted up by the emptiness of his own mind, cannot say, 'I believed, therefore I spoke'; since neither is it possible for him to bring in the next thing, 'But I was greatly humbled'; for he lives with conceit and boastfulness, and exults in empty words, not having acquired the strength that comes from faith. Then he humbles not only himself, but also all the humanity that is akin to him and shares his nature. 'For I said,' he says, 'in my ecstasy: Every man is a liar.' So that the one who is not helped by faith, but comes to speech from his own resources, trusting in human preparations for the comprehension of the truth, is a liar, falling far short of the truth. And he says that he said this word in ecstasy. What then is the ecstasy? Either that, having looked around at human nature, and having searched thoroughly, whether there is anywhere among human beings any truth, not being able to find it anywhere without the help from God, becoming astounded at the paradox of the matter, he cried out, 'Every man is a liar'; or in that ecstasy which I feigned before Achish, pretending epilepsy and derangement, since I saw myself coming into necessity of lying about myself, and of fabricating things that do not exist, in order to escape the danger from the enemies, then I said, 'Every man is a liar'; even if not by choice, nor for harm of neighbors, but in every case fleeing to lying because of certain circumstantial causes. The Prophet does not, however, fall into contradiction with himself according to the saying, as some of the sophistical arguers attempt to refute him, saying that the Prophet has fallen into the refutation by reversal. For if every man is a liar, and David is also a man, he too was clearly a liar; and if a liar, he must not be believed about the things he declares. And if this saying is not true, and not every man is a liar, we shall release David also from the charge of lying. But if he does not lie, let us believe him about the things he declares; and believing, we shall again be led around into the necessity of disbelieving. So that if David speaks truth, he dissolves his own saying, being both a man and not lying; but if he lies, he has from that very fact the not being believed; for who will pay attention to one who speaks falsely? So that since he once declared every man to be a liar, let David lie, in order to make the saying credible; or, speaking truth himself, he has dissolved the declaration.

choices.why: Keeps the vivid verb 'babble' for ληρέω and renders διά κενῆς as 'in vain' to preserve the sense of empty, purposeless speech.

choices.english: The beginning of rational discourse, then
choices.why: ἔμφρων means 'in one's right mind' or 'rational'; 'rational discourse' preserves the philosophical register Basil is using.

choices.english: going around the comprehension of God's essence
choices.why: περινοέω suggests circling around in thought; 'going around' keeps the spatial metaphor of attempting to grasp what cannot be grasped.
κοτύλη is a specific small liquid measure; 'small cup' conveys the concrete image of a tiny vessel against the whole sea.

choices.english: for he lives with conceit and boastfulness
choices.why: τῦφος is 'conceit' or 'vanity' and ἀλαζονεία is 'boastfulness'; the pair captures the inflated self-regard Basil is condemning.
περιτροπή means 'turning about' or 'reversal'; this is the technical term for the self-refuting argument the sophists use.

pass_b_english: In general, a soul that comes to speech without faith will babble in vain, driving its words forward with nothing beneath them. The beginning of rational discourse, then, is faith firmly established in the heart of the speaker. Next, he goes on to show how it is possible for us to accomplish faith perfectly, saying: “I was humbled greatly.” For the one who has not humbled his own mind, who does not say in imitation of the Apostle, “Brothers, I do not consider that I have yet laid hold of it” (Philippians 3:13), but instead pondering the comprehension of God’s essence, measuring out what cannot be reached with his own reasoning, and reckoning God to be only as great as his reasoning has encompassed—in short, the one who makes his own mind the measure of all things, not reckoning that it is easier to measure out the whole sea with a small cup than for the human mind to grasp the unutterable majesty of God—such a person is puffed up in vain and lifted up by the emptiness of his own mind. He cannot say, “I believed, therefore I spoke,” because he cannot add what follows: “I was humbled greatly.” For he lives with conceit and boastfulness, and exults in empty words, because he does not possess the strength that comes from faith.

Then he does not humble himself alone, but with himself all humanity that is akin to him and shares his nature. “I said in my ecstasy,” he says, “Every man is a liar” (Psalm 115:2 LXX; Psalm 116:11 Hebrew). So the one who is not helped by faith, but comes to speech from his own resources, trusting in human preparations for grasping the truth, is a liar, falling far short of the truth. And he says he spoke this word in ecstasy. What is the ecstasy? Either that, after looking around at human nature and searching carefully whether there is any truth among human beings, he could find it nowhere without help from God, and being struck with amazement at the strangeness of the matter, he cried out, “Every man is a liar.” Or it was in that ecstasy which he feigned before Achish, pretending epilepsy and derangement, when he saw that he had come to the necessity of lying about himself and inventing things that were not, in order to escape the danger from the enemies—then he said, “Every man is a liar.” Even if not by choice, nor for the harm of neighbors, still in every case he took refuge in lying because of some circumstantial causes.

The Prophet does not, however, fall into his own trap, as some of the sophistical arguers try to refute him, saying that the Prophet has fallen into the refutation by reversal. For if every man is a liar, and David is also a man, then clearly he too was a liar. And if he was a liar, he must not be believed in what he declares. But if this statement is not true, and not every man is a liar, then we will release David from the charge of lying. And if he does not lie, let us believe him in what he declares; but by believing him, we will again be driven around into the necessity of disbelieving. So if David speaks truth, he dissolves his own statement, since he is a man and does not lie. But if he lies, he has from that very fact the reason not to be believed—for who will pay attention to a liar? So since he once declared that every man is a liar, let David lie in order to confirm his statement; or if he himself speaks truth, he has destroyed his own declaration.

problems.why: Subject is David (masculine participle), but 'he' is ambiguous; more importantly, this continues David's voice, not a general statement.

problems.quote: goes around the comprehension of God's essence
problems.why: περινοῶν means 'thinking about/pondering', not 'going around'; the sense is pondering the comprehension of God's essence.
problems.fix: pondering the comprehension of God's essence
problems.ruling: περινοῶν means 'thinking about/pondering', not 'going around/circumventing'; meaning changed from intellectual presumption to mere contemplation.

problems.why: The Greek first person is David's voice in the psalm quotation, but English 'I' makes Basil the speaker; should be 'he'.
problems.ruling: First person ἐμαυτὸν is David's voice in Psalm context; Basil narrates, so 'I' misleads readers.

problems.quote: when I saw that I had come
problems.source_quote: ἐπειδὴ εἶδον εἰς ἀνάγκην ἐλθόντα ἐμαυτὸν
problems.why: Same issue: 'I saw' makes Basil the speaker, but this is David's voice in the psalm quotation.
problems.fix: when he saw that he had come
problems.ruling: εἶδον ἐμαυτὸν is David's first-person voice; English 'I' makes Basil speaker, misleading readers.

problems.why: Same issue: 'I said' should be 'he said' to maintain David as speaker in the psalm quotation.
problems.ruling: τότε εἶπον continues David's first-person; 'I said' makes Basil speaker, changing narrative voice.

edits.new: pondering the comprehension of God’s essence

edits.old: when I saw that I had come

Changed 'goes around the comprehension of God's essence' to 'pondering the comprehension of God's essence' to match περινοῶν.
Changed 'which I feigned before Achish' to 'which he feigned before Achish' to keep David as speaker.
Changed 'when I saw that I had come' to 'when he saw that he had come' to keep David as speaker.
Changed 'then I said' to 'then he said' to keep David as speaker.

problems.why: First person 'myself/my enemies' wrongly inserted; source has David speaking of himself in third person.

edits.old: lying about myself and inventing things that were not, in order to escape the danger from my enemies
edits.new: lying about himself and inventing things that were not, in order to escape the danger from the enemies

fixed: Changed first-person 'myself/my enemies' to third-person 'himself/the enemies' to match the source's third-person reference to David (καταψεύσασθαι ἐμαυτοῦ... ἀπὸ τῶν πολεμίων).

last_rejected.quote: driving its words forward with nothing beneath them
last_rejected.source_quote: κατ' οὐδενὸς ὑποκειμένου τὸν λόγον προάγουσα
last_rejected.why: Source says 'advancing speech against nothing underlying'; 'nothing beneath them' weakens the philosophical claim about lacking foundation.
last_rejected.fix: advancing its argument with no underlying reality to support it
last_rejected.ruling: 'Nothing beneath them' accurately renders κατ' οὐδενὸς ὑποκειμένου; both express lack of foundation.

last_rejected.quote: how it is possible for us to accomplish faith perfectly
last_rejected.source_quote: πόθεν ἡμῖν δυνατὸν τὸ περὶ τὴν πίστιν τέλειον κατορθοῦν
last_rejected.why: πόθεν means 'whence/from what source,' not 'how'; κατορθοῦν means 'to set right/establish,' not 'accomplish.'
last_rejected.fix: from what source it is possible for us to establish faith perfectly
last_rejected.ruling: πόθεν can mean 'how' in indirect questions; κατορθοῦν includes 'accomplish/succeed' — normal range.

last_rejected.quote: I do not consider that I have yet laid hold of it
last_rejected.why: The Apostle says 'I do not consider myself to have laid hold,' not 'laid hold of it'; the reflexive is crucial.
last_rejected.fix: I do not consider myself yet to have laid hold
last_rejected.ruling: 'Laid hold of it' correctly supplies the object from context; reflexive 'myself' is subject, not lost.

last_rejected.quote: not reckoning that it is easier
last_rejected.why: οὐ λογιζόμενος belongs to the subject ('not reckoning'), but the syntax makes this person the one who fails to reckon; 'not reckoning' obscures that this is a failure of the arrogant man.
last_rejected.fix: failing to reckon that it is easier
last_rejected.ruling: 'Not reckoning' correctly renders οὐ λογιζόμενος as a failure of the arrogant man; English syntax is clear.

last_rejected.quote: he lives with conceit and boastfulness
last_rejected.why: συζῇ means 'lives together with/is accompanied by,' not simply 'lives with'; the datives show companionship, not mere coexistence.
last_rejected.fix: for he is accompanied by conceit and boastfulness
last_rejected.ruling: 'Lives with' adequately renders συζῇ with dative; 'accompanied by' is preference, not error.

last_rejected.quote: Then he does not humble himself alone
last_rejected.why: οὐχ...μόνον means 'not only himself,' not 'does not humble himself alone'; the negation goes with μόνον, forming 'not only.'
last_rejected.fix: Then he humbles not only himself
last_rejected.ruling: 'Does not humble himself alone' correctly means 'not only himself'; οὐχ...μόνον negation is preserved.

last_rejected.why: The participles describe David's action, but the English 'he took refuge' makes it a completed action; the Greek shows ongoing circumstance, and the subject is David in the feigned madness.
last_rejected.ruling: Participle rendered as finite verb is normal English; ongoing vs completed aspect is minor preference.

last_rejected.why: περιπίπτει κατὰ τὸν λόγον means 'fall into contradiction in respect of the argument,' not 'trap'; 'trap' is too modern and metaphorical.
last_rejected.fix: fall into contradiction in his argument
last_rejected.ruling: 'Trap' is acceptable rendering of περιπίπτει κατὰ τὸν λόγον; 'fall into' preserves core meaning.

last_rejected.quote: saying that the Prophet has fallen into the refutation by reversal
last_rejected.source_quote: τῷ κατὰ περιτροπὴν ἐλέγχῳ ἐμπεπτωκέναι λέγοντες τὸν Προφήτην
last_rejected.why: ἐμπεπτωκέναι is perfect infinitive, 'to have fallen'; the English present 'has fallen' misses that this is the sophists' claim about a completed fall.
last_rejected.fix: saying that the Prophet has fallen into refutation by reversal
last_rejected.ruling: English 'has fallen' is natural rendering of perfect infinitive; perfect aspect is preserved in context.

last_rejected.quote: we will again be driven around into the necessity of disbelieving
last_rejected.source_quote: πάλιν εἰς τὴν τοῦ ἀπιστεῖν ἀνάγκην περιαχθησόμεθα
last_rejected.why: περιαχθησόμεθα is passive future, 'we shall be led around'; 'driven around' is too violent, and the sense is circular reasoning leading back to disbelief.
last_rejected.fix: we shall again be led around into the necessity of disbelieving
last_rejected.ruling: 'Driven around' for περιαχθησόμεθα is within normal range; circular reasoning sense is preserved.

last_rejected.quote: let David lie in order to confirm his statement
last_rejected.source_quote: ψευδέσθω Δαβίδ, ἵνα τὸν λόγον πιστώσηται
last_rejected.why: πιστώσηται is middle, 'make credible/confirm for himself,' but the English 'confirm his statement' loses the reflexive nuance of self-confirmation through lying.
last_rejected.fix: let David lie, so that he may confirm his statement for himself
last_rejected.ruling: Middle πιστώσηται rendered 'confirm his statement' preserves meaning; reflexive nuance is minor, not lost.
